LanguageData.CC_TownLife_FightText: The colony's fighters have reached {TOWN}: {NAMES}. {ENEMY} are coming in at the far side of the town, and {PEOPLE} are on their walls.\n\nIt is their town now, and the colony's fighters fight beside its people, not over them. Every raider down or gone, and {TOWN} stands.
LanguageData.CC_TownLife_RaidDeadNote: The colony's former people there lost {DEAD} in the fighting.
LanguageData.CC_TownLife_FightFormers: The colony's former people at {TOWN} are among its defenders: {NAMES}.
LanguageData.CC_TownLife_FightLayout: The town is {COLONY} as the colony left it: the same walls, the same doors, the same rooms.
LanguageData.CC_TownLife_DiedHistory: {PAWN}, one of the colony's own once, died at {TOWN}.
LanguageData.CC_TownLife_HardshipText: Word from {TOWN} by {MEANS}: {PAWN}, one of the colony's own once, has died {WHAT}.\n\n{TOWN}, the town {COLONY} was, mourns them.
LanguageData.CC_TownLife_HardshipHelped: What the colony sent {TOWN} in that time is remembered there; without it, more would have died.
LanguageData.CC_TownLife_CooledHead: a head who thinks little of {COLONY}
LanguageData.CC_TownLife_CoolHead: {HEAD} leads {TOWN} now as its {TITLE}, and has little good to say of {COLONY}. The town will be cooler to the colony while they lead it.
LanguageData.CC_TownLife_AskBackText: Word from {TOWN} by {MEANS}: {HEAD} asks whether the colony would take its old town back. {PEOPLE} have had a hard time of it, and would rather be {COLONY}'s again than go on alone.
LanguageData.CC_TownLife_AskBackForm: Taken back, it is the colony's again by {FORM}: its map as the colony left it, its former colonists the colony's people again, and some of its other people with them.
LanguageData.CC_TownLife_AskBackAgain: It is not the first time {TOWN} has asked. If the colony says no again, its people may not stay there much longer.
LanguageData.CC_TownLife_AskLapsed: {TOWN} had no answer from the colony, and took the silence as a no.
LanguageData.CC_TownLife_Leaving: The people of {TOWN} are giving up the town {COLONY} was. Some of them are on the road to the colony.
LanguageData.CC_TownLife_GateText: {PEOPLE} have given up {TOWN}. The town {COLONY} was stands empty, a ruin on the map.
LanguageData.CC_TownLife_GateFormers: The colony's former people from {COLONY} are coming to the colony's gate to ask to come home: {NAMES}.
LanguageData.CC_TownLife_GateOthers: Of the rest of {PEOPLE}, {NAMES} would rather join the colony than go elsewhere, and are coming to the gate.
LanguageData.CC_TownLife_GateLast: {TOWN} was all {PEOPLE} had. They are no longer a people of their own.
LanguageData.CC_TownLife_GateNotLast: The rest of {PEOPLE} have gone on to their other towns.
LanguageData.CC_TownLife_GateAsk: They will wait at the gate for the colony's answer.
LanguageData.CC_TownLife_Choice_Ours: Take in only those who were {COLONY}'s
LanguageData.CC_TownLife_GateIn: {NAMES} are the colony's people again, home from {TOWN}.
LanguageData.CC_TownLife_GateOn: The people from {TOWN} have gone on their way.
LanguageData.CC_TownLife_GivenUpHistory: {PEOPLE} gave up {TOWN}, the town the colony was, and some of them came to the colony's gate.
LanguageData.CC_TownLife_Growing: {PEOPLE} of {TOWN}, the town {COLONY} was, have begun building a new town of their own.
LanguageData.CC_TownLife_Grew: {PEOPLE} have finished {NEWTOWN}, a new town of theirs grown from {TOWN}.
LanguageData.CC_TownLife_RaidFormer: Among the raiders is {NAMES}, one of the colony's own once, who lived at {TOWN}, the town {COLONY} was.
LanguageData.CC_TownLife_RaidFormers: Among the raiders are {NAMES}, the colony's own once, who lived at {TOWN}, the town {COLONY} was.
LanguageData.CC_Memory_Deed_townDefended: stood on their walls when raiders came to the town the colony was
